sources.title: Global Convergence Analysis of the Power Proximal Point and Augmented Lagrangian Method
conditions: p >= 1; Euclidean or designated lp+1 norm power prox
uniform gap growth c*d^nu on a neighborhood of entire minimizer set, nu > 1
bounded initial sublevel in surrounding analysis; coercive mapped objective supplies this
sources.mapping: Fully applicable to constant-SPD C272 normal quotient via eta=A^-1/2 B_m(u), Psi=m/(m+1)||A^1/2 eta||^((m+1)/m), p=1 and nu=1+1/m. Physical order follows explicit power norm comparisons.
sources.limits: Not a direct theorem import for the general state-dependent nonconvex C1 full stationary relation; ALM-specific strong duality is not needed for Section 3.

sources.title: Convergence of descent methods for semi-algebraic and tame problems: proximal algorithms, forward-backward splitting, and regularized Gauss-Seidel methods
conditions: uniform positive quadratic sufficient decrease H1
value-continuous cluster point H3 for Theorem 2.9
Theorem 2.12 instead uses local initialization at global minimizer and H1-H2
sources.mapping: Every C272 C1 full stationary trajectory in small invariant strip satisfies all conditions for E(u,z)=||u||^2. Constants and noncircular H3 proof supplied in report. NG12 also admits original-f H1/H2/KL.
sources.limits: The energy construction uses known flat zero coordinates and previously derived full-output bounds. It does not imply arbitrary C249 models admit such a smooth energy.

sources.title: Anisotropic Proximal Point Algorithm
sources.version: arXiv:2312.09834v4, submitted 2025-12-29; read current PDF header 2025-12-30
conditions: inherited maximal monotone operator and nonempty zeros
smooth strictly convex supercoercive full-domain prox with gradient zero at zero
Eq4.16 with summable errors and selected error exponent
all near-limit graph pairs with point and value truncations satisfy d<=rho||value||^nu
sources.mapping: Fully applicable to constant-SPD transformed convex normal operator lambda*grad(Psi), quadratic prox p=2, higher-order EB nu=m, zero errors. General C272 transformed T has ordinary m-subregularity but can be nonmonotone.
sources.limits: Exact frozen PDF endpoint failed; read PDF header and arXiv version bar freeze identity. Statement that Prop4.8 specializes Luque1986 is a fact about this paper, not verification of Luque original.

sources.title: Asymptotic Convergence Analysis of a New Class of Proximal Point Methods
sources.version: SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization 46 (2007), 1683-1704; DOI 10.1137/060666627; read 22-page published PDF
conditions: local quadratic growth at a minimizer
C2 objective with Lipschitz Hessian locally
C1/C2 acceptance includes F_k(x_next)<=f(x_k) and specified residual bound
sources.mapping: Positive historical comparator for nonisolated-minimum point convergence and superlinear distance order; no same-algorithm direct import asserted.
sources.limits: C272 mixed flat-normal/identity-tangent kernel is not the paper's scalar quadratic regularization. General C1 C272 does not inherit Lipschitz-Hessian assumptions.

sources.title: Higher-Order Metric Subregularity and Its Applications
conditions: ordinary q-subregularity uses distance to full zero fiber
strong q-subregularity uses distance to specified point
sources.mapping: General C272 kernel-space relation has ordinary global q=m subregularity; nonisolated zeros prevent automatic strong-subregularity import.
sources.limits: This report does not claim its Newton theorem is a full-stationary PPA theorem.

sources.title: Fast convergence to non-isolated minima: four equivalent conditions for C2 functions

explicit neighborhood/constant loss for EB/QG/PL implications

sources.limits: No assertion of a C1 MB equivalence.

sources.title: Asymptotic convergence analysis of high-order proximal-point methods beyond sublinear rates
sources.version: arXiv:2505.20484v2, 2026-07-29; 30-page PDF; HTML theorem34 corresponds to PDF theorem4.9
conditions: uniform quasiconvexity on closed convex feasible set inside effective domain
gamma_k bounded between fixed positive thresholds
global modulus lower bound rho_q*t^q, q>=2
unique minimizing point follows uniform quasiconvexity
